explanation.whyCorrect: Listeriolysin O helps the bacterium avoid digestion in phagosomes after host cell entry via phagocytosis. Its mechanism is host cell membrane disruption, which is also why the organism lyses erythrocytes and appears hemolytic on blood agar. Escaping into the cytosol is the step that permits the organism to survive as a facultative intracellular pathogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ActA mediates intracellular movement through actin polymerization only after the organism has already reached the cytosol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Catalase is a metabolic enzyme used for laboratory identification and is not the factor described as mediating phagosomal escape.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flagellin builds flagella for extracellular tumbling motility and has no role in breaching the phagosomal membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Internalin A mediates attachment to and invasion of host cells, a step that occurs before the organism is inside a phagosome.

questions.stem: A mutant strain of Listeria monocytogenes is constructed in the laboratory. When macrophages are infected with it, the bacteria remain confined within phagosomes and are degraded. Loss of which of the following pairs of products best explains this phenotype?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Internalin A and internalin B proteins

explanation.summary: Listeriolysin O and phospholipase C together allow Listeria to break out of the phagosome after being ingested.
explanation.whyCorrect: Listeriolysin O and phospholipase C enzymes help the bacteria avoid digestion in phagosomes following host cell entry via phagocytosis. Both act by disrupting host cell membranes. A mutant lacking both would be taken up normally but would be trapped and destroyed inside the phagosome, exactly the phenotype described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ActA and flagellin govern movement inside and outside the cell; their loss would impair spread but would not trap the organism in a phagosome.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Catalase and superoxide dismutase are not the factors this brick identifies as mediating phagosomal escape in Listeria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Coagulase and protein A are staphylococcal products and are not produced by Listeria monocytogenes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Internalins mediate adhesion and invasion, so their loss would reduce entry into host cells rather than block escape after uptake.

questions.stem: After contaminated food is swallowed, Listeria monocytogenes must attach to and invade the enterocytes lining the gastrointestinal epithelium before it can reach the circulation. Which of the following bacterial surface proteins mediates this adhesion and invasion step?

explanation.summary: Internalin surface proteins mediate Listeria adhesion to and invasion of host cells, including enterocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Internalins are the surface proteins that allow L. monocytogenes to adhere to and invade the GI epithelium. Internalin A targets enterocytes, while internalin B targets endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and enterocytes. This invasion of the gut lining is the second step in the pathway from ingestion of contaminated food to dissemination.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ActA drives propulsion through the cytosol by actin polymerization after the organism is already inside a cell.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Flagellin builds the flagella responsible for extracellular tumbling motility and does not mediate host cell invasion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Listeriolysin O disrupts the phagosomal membrane after uptake rather than mediating initial attachment to enterocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phospholipase C also acts on host membranes to permit phagosomal escape and is not an adhesion protein.

questions.stem: A 73-year-old man has a 1-day history of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He has vomited four times today. He recently visited his son's farm, where he drank several glasses of fresh milk taken directly from the farm's supply. Examination shows mild generalized abdominal tenderness. There is no blood in the stool. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

explanation.summary: Unpasteurized dairy is a classic vehicle for Listeria monocytogenes, which pasteurization would otherwise kill.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common route of transmission for L. monocytogenes is ingestion of contaminated food, and unpasteurized dairy products are a leading source. Routine pasteurization at commercial dairies kills the organism, so fresh farm milk that has not been pasteurized is the exposure that stands out here. In an older adult the resulting illness can be more severe than the mild gastroenteritis seen in healthy adults.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bacillus cereus food poisoning is classically linked to reheated fried rice, not to unpasteurized milk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clostridioides difficile colitis follows antibiotic exposure with disruption of colonic flora, which this patient does not report.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Norovirus spreads person to person or through contaminated shared food and would not be specifically tied to raw farm milk.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vibrio parahaemolyticus gastroenteritis follows ingestion of raw or undercooked seafood rather than dairy.

questions.stem: A microbiologist preparing an environmental sampling plan asks where Listeria monocytogenes is most commonly found outside of infected patients. Which of the following best describes the organism's natural distribution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arthropod vectors such as ticks, fleas, and mosquitoes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hospital water systems and air-conditioning cooling towers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Soil, water, plant life, and the feces of animal carriers

choices.label: D
choices.text: The human nasopharynx, with no environmental reservoir

choices.label: E
choices.text: The intestinal tract of shellfish and other marine animals

explanation.summary: Listeria monocytogenes is abundant in the general environment and in animal carriers, including humans.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes is abundant in the environment and can be found in plant life, soil, water, and animal carriers, including humans. It can also be isolated from animal feces, and humans may carry a low level of the organism as gastrointestinal flora. This wide environmental distribution explains how the organism repeatedly enters the food supply.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Listeria is acquired by ingestion of contaminated food or vertically, not through arthropod vectors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Water systems and cooling towers are the reservoir for Legionella, not for Listeria monocytogenes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Listeria is not a nasopharyngeal colonizer, and it has an extensive environmental reservoir in soil, water, and plants.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Shellfish are not the defining reservoir; the organism is widespread in terrestrial environments and farm animals.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 28 weeks' gestation asks which foods she should avoid to lower her risk of listeriosis. Which of the following foods carries the greatest risk?

explanation.summary: Susceptible patients should avoid soft cheeses, unpasteurized milk, processed meats, and raw vegetables.
explanation.whyCorrect: Soft cheeses are among the foods most often implicated in listeriosis, along with unpasteurized dairy products, processed meats, and raw vegetables. Patients at increased risk, including pregnant people, are specifically advised to avoid these items. Brie is a soft cheese and is therefore the highest-risk food on this list.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Canned tuna is commercially heat-processed and is not among the implicated ready-to-eat or dairy vehicles.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Freshly cooked rice is not a recognized vehicle for Listeria and is not on the list of foods susceptible patients should avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hard-boiled eggs are thoroughly cooked and are not a recognized source of listeriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pasteurization kills Listeria, so a pasteurized dairy product is a low-risk choice rather than a food to avoid.

questions.stem: An infection-control team investigates a cluster of listeriosis traced to ready-to-eat meats that were fully cooked at the plant and then held under continuous refrigeration until sale. Which of the following properties of the organism best explains its persistence in this product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Formation of heat-resistant endospores in dry conditions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Growth across a broad range of temperature, pH, and salt

choices.label: C
choices.text: Production of a thick antiphagocytic polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strictly anaerobic metabolism inside sealed packaging

choices.label: E
choices.text: Survival restricted to the interior of host macrophages

explanation.summary: Listeria tolerates wide swings in temperature, pH, and salinity, so it persists in cooked, refrigerated foods.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes exhibits growth across a broad range of temperatures, pH values, and salt content. This tolerance is exactly what enables the bacteria to persist even in cooked, refrigerated foods, where most pathogens would be held in check. Refrigeration, salting, and acidification therefore do not make a ready-to-eat product safe once it is contaminated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Listeria does not form endospores; its survival depends on vegetative growth under harsh physical conditions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A polysaccharide capsule is not the feature described as letting Listeria survive refrigeration and salting.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The organism is facultative rather than strictly anaerobic, and anaerobiosis would not explain growth in a refrigerated product.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Listeria can live freely in soil, water, and food and is not restricted to an intracellular niche.

questions.stem: A county health department is reviewing occupational exposures to a foodborne pathogen carried by farm animals. Workers in which of the following occupations are at increased risk of exposure to Listeria monocytogenes?

explanation.summary: Occupations with heavy animal and raw-food contact carry increased Listeria exposure risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Certain occupations carry higher risk because of increased exposure to the organism, including butchers, farmers, veterinarians, slaughterhouse workers, poultry farmers, and fish mongers. Veterinarians handle animal carriers and animal feces, both recognized reservoirs for L. monocytogenes. Health care roles without animal or raw-food contact do not carry this occupational risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dental hygienists have no routine contact with farm animals or raw animal food products.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pharmacy technicians work with packaged medications and have no recognized occupational Listeria exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Physical therapists have no exposure pathway to the animal and food reservoirs of this organism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiologic technologists have no occupational contact with animal carriers or contaminated food.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 22 weeks' gestation asks how her risk of listeriosis compares with that of the general population. Which of the following best answers her question?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her risk is roughly 10 times as high

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her risk is roughly 2 times as high

choices.label: C
choices.text: Her risk is roughly 5 times as high

choices.label: D
choices.text: Her risk is roughly half as high

choices.label: E
choices.text: Her risk is the same as the general population

explanation.summary: Pregnant people are about 10 times more likely to get listeriosis than the general population.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnant people are 10 times more likely to get listeriosis than the general population. This is why pregnancy is grouped with the neonatal period, advanced age, and immunocompromise as a state of special susceptibility. The magnitude of the increase is what justifies specific dietary counseling in prenatal care.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A twofold increase substantially understates the excess risk documented in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A fivefold increase is still well below the roughly tenfold figure reported for pregnant people.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pregnancy increases rather than decreases susceptibility to L. monocytogenes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pregnancy is one of the defining high-risk states for listeriosis, so risk is clearly not equal to baseline.

questions.stem: A pregnant patient is being counseled about listeriosis. During which of the following periods is she most susceptible to Listeria monocytogenes infection?

explanation.summary: Pregnant patients are most susceptible to Listeria infection in the third trimester.
explanation.whyCorrect: Changes in cellular immunity over the course of pregnancy reach their greatest effect in the third trimester, which is when these patients are most susceptible to L. monocytogenes infection. Because Listeria is a facultative intracellular organism, cell-mediated immunity is the arm of host defense that matters most. Counseling about high-risk foods is therefore especially important late in pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: First-trimester infection can cause spontaneous abortion, but susceptibility to acquiring infection peaks later in gestation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The postpartum week is not identified as the period of greatest susceptibility to acquiring Listeria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Before conception the patient has no pregnancy-associated change in cellular immunity and is at general-population risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The second trimester is an intermediate period and is not the point of maximal susceptibility.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation has a 2-day history of fever, myalgias, and arthralgias that began after she ate sliced deli meat. She has no headache, neck stiffness, or altered mental status. Blood cultures grow Listeria monocytogenes. Which of the following best describes the expected course of the mother's own illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A mild, nonspecific, self-limiting flu-like illness

choices.label: C
choices.text: Necrotizing soft-tissue infection of the abdominal wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Toxic shock with desquamating rash and hypotension

explanation.summary: In pregnant patients, listeriosis typically causes only a mild, self-limited flu-like illness in the mother.
explanation.whyCorrect: In pregnant people, the resulting illness from L. monocytogenes is typically mild, nonspecific, and self-limiting, with fever, myalgias, and arthralgias. The clinical danger in pregnancy lies less with the mother than with transplacental spread to the fetus. This mismatch is why a seemingly trivial febrile illness in pregnancy still warrants attention.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fulminant hepatic failure is not a described presentation of maternal listeriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Necrotizing soft-tissue infection is not a manifestation of Listeria infection in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Meningitis is the pattern seen in neonates, the elderly, and patients with defective cellular immunity rather than in the pregnant patient herself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Toxic shock with desquamation is a toxin-mediated staphylococcal or streptococcal syndrome, not maternal listeriosis.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 11 weeks' gestation is diagnosed with listeriosis after eating unpasteurized soft cheese. She is counseled about possible outcomes of the pregnancy. Which of the following is she at greatest risk for?

explanation.summary: Listeria crosses the placenta, and infection early in pregnancy can cause spontaneous abortion, stillbirth, or premature birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes can be transmitted transplacentally. If infection occurs early in the pregnancy, it may cause spontaneous abortion, stillbirth, or premature birth. Vertical transmission is a recognized route of acquisition for this organism, in addition to ingestion of contaminated food.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congenital cataracts are characteristic of congenital rubella rather than of intrauterine Listeria infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Limb reduction defects follow teratogen exposure such as varicella embryopathy and are not a Listeria outcome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neural tube defects arise from folate deficiency and early neurulation errors, not from maternal bacteremia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sensorineural hearing loss is a classic sequela of congenital cytomegalovirus or rubella infection.

questions.stem: A newborn delivered at 33 weeks' gestation has respiratory distress at birth and dies within hours. The mother had a febrile illness with myalgias late in pregnancy. Autopsy shows disseminated granulomas and small abscesses throughout the liver, spleen, and lungs. Which of the following is the name of this condition?

explanation.summary: Granulomatosis infantiseptica is the severe early-onset form of neonatal listeriosis with disseminated granulomas and abscesses.
explanation.whyCorrect: A severe form of early-onset disease in the newborn may present as disseminated granulomas and abscesses in multiple organs, a condition called granulomatosis infantiseptica. It follows transplacental transmission from a mother who often had only a mild flu-like illness. The multiorgan granulomatous and suppurative pattern at autopsy is the defining feature.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congenital rubella syndrome causes cardiac defects, cataracts, and deafness rather than disseminated pyogenic granulomas.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythroblastosis fetalis results from maternal-fetal blood group incompatibility with hemolysis, not from bacterial abscesses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hydrops fetalis describes abnormal fluid accumulation in fetal compartments and has many noninfectious causes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Necrotizing enterocolitis is a bowel-limited ischemic and inflammatory disease of preterm infants, usually developing days after birth.

questions.stem: A 12-day-old infant born at term after an uncomplicated delivery develops fever, poor feeding, and a bulging fontanelle. Cerebrospinal fluid culture grows gram-positive rods. Which of the following best characterizes this presentation?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Late-onset neonatal disease presenting as meningitis

explanation.summary: Late-onset neonatal listeriosis appears after birth as meningitis, meningoencephalitis, or septicemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Late-onset disease in a neonate presents after birth and is characterized by meningitis, meningoencephalitis, or septicemia. A term infant who was well at delivery and presents near two weeks of age with fever and a bulging fontanelle fits this pattern. Recovery of gram-positive rods from CSF points to L. monocytogenes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Febrile gastroenteritis is the presentation seen in healthy nonpregnant adults, not in a neonate with CSF findings.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Early-onset disease presents at or shortly after birth with disseminated granulomas and abscesses, not with isolated meningitis at 12 days.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stillbirth follows infection early in pregnancy, which is incompatible with a liveborn term infant presenting two weeks later.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This infant was delivered at term after an uncomplicated pregnancy, so premature birth from intrauterine infection does not apply.

questions.stem: A previously healthy 28-year-old man has fever and watery diarrhea that began 1 day after he ate raw bean sprouts at a restaurant. He is not pregnant or immunocompromised and takes no medications. Stool culture grows Listeria monocytogenes. Which of the following best describes the expected course of his illness?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Progression to meningitis in most patients

explanation.summary: In healthy nonpregnant adults, listeriosis is a mild, self-limited febrile gastroenteritis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Healthy adults may acquire a transient L. monocytogenes infection characterized as a febrile gastroenteritis with diarrhea. This gastroenteritis is usually mild and self-limited in healthy nonpregnant adults. Severe invasive disease is reserved for neonates, pregnant people, the elderly, and patients with defective cellular immunity.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic carriage with relapsing fever is not a described pattern of Listeria infection in healthy adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hemolytic uremic syndrome follows Shiga toxin-producing organisms such as enterohemorrhagic E. coli, not Listeria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Infective endocarditis is not the expected outcome of transient Listeria gastroenteritis in a healthy host.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Meningitis is a manifestation in neonates, elderly patients, and the immunocompromised, not the usual course in a healthy young adult.

questions.stem: Five patients are seen in a general medicine clinic on the same afternoon. Which of the following patients is at greatest risk for severe invasive listeriosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 9-year-old boy with seasonal allergic rhinitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 35-year-old man with iron deficiency anemia

choices.label: E
choices.text: A 58-year-old man 3 months after renal transplantation

explanation.summary: Defective cellular immunity, as after transplantation, is the key risk factor for severe listeriosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with defects in cellular immunity, including those with AIDS, lymphomas, or a history of transplant, develop listeriosis that is more severe than in healthy adults. A recent transplant recipient on immunosuppression falls squarely in this group. L. monocytogenes is also the most common cause of meningitis in transplant patients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allergic rhinitis does not impair cell-mediated immunity, and healthy children have only milder disease presentations.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Well-controlled asthma is not a state of defective cellular immunity and does not predispose to invasive listeriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Iron deficiency anemia does not produce the T-cell defect that underlies severe Listeria infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mild hypothyroidism has no effect on cell-mediated immunity or on susceptibility to this organism.

questions.stem: Which of the following patient populations is least at risk for acquiring a severe Listeria monocytogenes infection?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neonates in the first month of life

choices.label: E
choices.text: People in the third trimester of pregnancy

explanation.summary: Severe listeriosis is concentrated in neonates, pregnant people, the elderly, and the immunocompromised.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes infections typically cause severe disease only in a few patient populations: neonates, pregnant people, the elderly, and the immunocompromised, particularly those with defective cellular immunity. Healthy adults and children are susceptible to milder disease presentations. A healthy nonpregnant adult is therefore the least likely to develop severe invasive infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Listeriosis in elderly patients is more severe than in healthy adults, placing them in a high-risk group.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neonates are a defining high-risk population, with early-onset and late-onset forms of severe disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: AIDS produces defective cellular immunity, the specific defect that predisposes to severe listeriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pregnant people are roughly 10 times more likely to get listeriosis than the general population.

questions.stem: A transplant center reviews every case of bacterial meningitis that occurred in its solid-organ transplant recipients over the past decade. Which of the following organisms is the most common cause of meningitis in this patient population?

explanation.summary: Listeria monocytogenes is the most common cause of meningitis in transplant patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes is the most common cause of meningitis in transplant patients. Transplant recipients have defective cellular immunity, the arm of the immune system needed to control a facultative intracellular organism. Recognizing this association matters clinically, because standard empiric meningitis regimens may not cover Listeria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cryptococcus neoformans is a fungus and is not the most common bacterial cause of meningitis in this group.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Haemophilus influenzae type b meningitis has become uncommon and is a disease of unimmunized young children.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neisseria meningitidis predominantly causes meningitis in adolescents and young adults in community settings.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a leading cause of meningitis in the general adult population but not the top cause after transplant.

questions.stem: Patients with defects in cellular immunity, such as those with AIDS, lymphoma, or a prior organ transplant, have disproportionately severe listeriosis compared with healthy adults. Which of the following features of Listeria monocytogenes best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It forms endospores that resist host enzymatic attack

choices.label: B
choices.text: It produces an antiphagocytic polysaccharide capsule

choices.label: C
choices.text: It secretes an exotoxin that inactivates elongation factor 2

choices.label: D
choices.text: It survives and replicates as a facultative intracellular organism

choices.label: E
choices.text: It undergoes rapid antigenic variation of its major surface proteins

explanation.summary: Listeria is a facultative intracellular organism, so control depends on cell-mediated immunity.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes is a facultative intracellular rod. After phagocytosis it uses listeriolysin O and phospholipase C to escape the phagosome and then spreads cell to cell using ActA-driven actin rockets, staying largely out of reach of antibody. Clearing an organism that lives inside host cells requires cell-mediated immunity, which is exactly what is impaired in AIDS, lymphoma, and transplant recipients.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Listeria does not form endospores, so spore resistance cannot explain its behavior in immunocompromised hosts.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An antiphagocytic capsule is not the feature Listeria relies on; the organism is in fact taken up by phagocytes and then escapes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inactivation of elongation factor 2 is the mechanism of diphtheria and Pseudomonas exotoxins, not a Listeria virulence factor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rapid antigenic variation is a strategy of organisms such as Neisseria gonorrhoeae and is not described for Listeria.

questions.stem: An 80-year-old woman with bacterial meningitis is treated empirically with ceftriaxone and vancomycin but does not improve over 48 hours. Cerebrospinal fluid culture then grows a catalase-positive, weakly beta-hemolytic gram-positive rod. Which of the following best explains the failure of the cephalosporin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ceftriaxone does not achieve adequate CSF concentrations

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dosing interval was too long for a time-dependent agent

choices.label: C
choices.text: The isolate carries an altered penicillin-binding protein 2a

choices.label: D
choices.text: The isolate produces an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism is inherently resistant to cephalosporins

explanation.summary: Listeria monocytogenes is inherently resistant to cephalosporins, so ceftriaxone fails regardless of dose.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes is inherently resistant to several classes of antibiotics, including cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, and tetracycline. This resistance is intrinsic to the species rather than acquired, so no cephalosporin will treat the infection. The catalase-positive, weakly beta-hemolytic gram-positive rod recovered from CSF in an elderly patient identifies the organism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ceftriaxone penetrates inflamed meninges well and is a standard agent for other causes of bacterial meningitis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A dosing error would not account for a species that is resistant to the entire cephalosporin class.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Altered penicillin-binding protein 2a is the mechanism of methicillin resistance in staphylococci, which are cocci rather than rods.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An acquired extended-spectrum beta-lactamase is not needed to explain the failure, since resistance to cephalosporins is intrinsic to this species.

questions.stem: Listeria monocytogenes is inherently resistant to several classes of antibiotics. Which of the following classes should therefore not be relied on to treat an invasive Listeria infection?

explanation.summary: Listeria is intrinsically resistant to fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, macrolides, and tetracycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: L. monocytogenes is inherently resistant to several classes of antibiotics, including fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, macrolides, and tetracycline. Fluoroquinolone resistance is the best characterized of these and is attributed largely to efflux pumps. These agents should not be used to treat invasive Listeria infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aminoglycosides such as gentamicin are used to supplement ampicillin therapy rather than avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminopenicillins are the treatment of choice, since ampicillin is the drug of choice for L. monocytogenes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycopeptides are not among the classes listed as targets of the organism's intrinsic resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole has been proven effective, particularly in cases of antibiotic resistance.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man is admitted with fever and hypotension. Blood cultures grow Listeria monocytogenes. Which of the following is the drug of choice for treating this infection?

explanation.summary: Ampicillin is the drug of choice for Listeria monocytogenes infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: The drug of choice for the treatment of L. monocytogenes is ampicillin. It may be supplemented with gentamicin in serious infection. The other major antibiotic classes are unreliable because the organism is inherently resistant to them.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Azithromycin is a macrolide, a class to which Listeria is inherently resistant.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ceftriaxone is a cephalosporin, and Listeria is inherently resistant to this entire class.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone, the class for which the organism's efflux-pump resistance is best characterized.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Doxycycline is a tetracycline, another class covered by the organism's inherent resistance.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old woman is started on ampicillin for Listeria monocytogenes meningitis. Which of the following agents is most commonly added to supplement this therapy?

explanation.summary: Ampicillin for listeriosis may be supplemented with gentamicin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ampicillin is the drug of choice for L. monocytogenes and may be supplemented with gentamicin, particularly in serious invasive infection such as meningitis or bacteremia. The combination is standard practice in high-risk patients. Susceptible patients are additionally advised to avoid milk, soft cheeses, processed meats, and raw vegetables.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clindamycin targets anaerobes and gram-positive cocci and is not the agent paired with ampicillin for listeriosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythromycin is a macrolide, a class to which Listeria is inherently resistant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole is active against anaerobes and protozoa and has no role against this facultative organism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rifampin is used for mycobacterial disease and selected staphylococcal infections, not as the standard Listeria adjunct.

questions.stem: A Listeria monocytogenes isolate from a septic patient is found to carry movable genetic elements that confer resistance to penicillin and ampicillin. Which of the following agents has been shown to be effective in this situation?

explanation.summary: When Listeria is resistant to penicillin and ampicillin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is an effective alternative.
explanation.whyCorrect: Recent research has shown that L. monocytogenes bacteria have movable genetic elements that confer increasing resistance to penicillin and ampicillin. In cases of antibiotic resistance, the use of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole has been proven effective in treating an L. monocytogenes infection. It is the recognized fallback when the first-line aminopenicillins cannot be used.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cephalosporins such as cefepime fail because Listeria is inherently resistant to this entire class.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fluoroquinolones such as levofloxacin are the class the organism resists most characteristically, through efflux pumps.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Macrolides such as clarithromycin are another class covered by the organism's intrinsic resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tetracyclines such as doxycycline are also on the list of classes to which Listeria is inherently resistant.

questions.stem: Among the several mechanisms of antibiotic resistance used by Listeria species, one is the best understood and accounts in particular for the organism's resistance to fluoroquinolones. Which of the following is that mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Active export of the drug by efflux pumps

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mutation of the drug's target site

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced uptake from changes in membrane permeability

explanation.summary: Efflux pumps are the best-understood resistance mechanism in Listeria and underlie fluoroquinolone resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The best understood mechanism by which Listeria spp. demonstrate antibiotic resistance is through use of efflux pumps, which actively excrete the drug from the bacterial cell. This is particularly true of their resistance to fluoroquinolones. Other general mechanisms exist in bacteria, but efflux is the one specifically characterized in this organism.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemical modification of a drug is another recognized bacterial strategy, yet it is not the mechanism tied to Listeria fluoroquinolone resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Enzymatic cleavage, such as beta-lactamase activity, is a general bacterial mechanism but not the one best characterized in Listeria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Modification of the drug target occurs in many bacteria but is not identified as the best-understood mechanism here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Decreased uptake through altered membrane permeability is a general mechanism and is not what explains this organism's fluoroquinolone resistance.

questions.stem: Surveillance data show increasing resistance of Listeria monocytogenes to penicillin and ampicillin, the drugs classically used against it. Which of the following best accounts for this trend?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion to a dormant endospore form

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of porin channels in the cell envelope

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overproduction of catalase under oxidative stress

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spontaneous mutation of ribosomal binding sites

explanation.summary: Movable genetic elements are driving increasing penicillin and ampicillin resistance in Listeria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Recent research has demonstrated that L. monocytogenes bacteria have movable genetic elements that confer increasing resistance to penicillin and ampicillin. Because these drugs are the mainstay of therapy, this trend is clinically important, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is the alternative in resistant cases. Movable elements also allow resistance to spread between organisms rather than arising anew in each strain.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Listeria does not form endospores, so dormancy cannot explain rising ampicillin resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Porin loss reduces drug entry in gram-negative organisms; Listeria is a gram-positive rod without that outer membrane.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Catalase is used for laboratory identification and does not confer beta-lactam resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ribosomal binding site mutations affect protein synthesis inhibitors, not cell wall-active penicillins.

questions.stem: One hypothesis links the unusually broad antibiotic resistance of Listeria monocytogenes to the environment the organism occupies outside the human body. Which of the following statements best expresses this hypothesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Human intestinal flora transfer resistance genes during asymptomatic carriage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marine bacteriophages carry resistance genes into the commercial seafood supply

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prophylactic antibiotics in livestock select for resistant bacteria in food

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refrigerated storage of food induces expression of resistance genes in the organism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ultraviolet light in surface soil mutates the genes that regulate drug uptake

explanation.summary: Heavy prophylactic antibiotic use in livestock selects for resistant bacteria that then contaminate food.
explanation.whyCorrect: Listeria spp. are frequently found in unpasteurized dairy products and processed meats. Many agriculturally raised animals are given very high prophylactic doses of antibiotics in the hope of reducing contamination of animal food products, and this consistently selects for antibiotic resistance. When bacteria from livestock contaminate produce, they are commonly antibiotic resistant, which links the organism's food-associated niche to its broad resistance profile.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Humans may carry a low level of Listeria as gut flora, but gene transfer from human flora is not the stated hypothesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Seafood and bacteriophage transfer are not part of the explanation offered for Listeria antibiotic resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cold tolerance explains why the organism survives refrigeration, but refrigeration is not proposed as the driver of drug resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ultraviolet-induced mutation in soil is not the proposed explanation for this organism's resistance profile.

questions.stem: A public health officer is summarizing the annual burden of listeriosis in the United States for a hospital grand rounds. Approximately how many people contract the illness each year, and approximately how many die of it?

explanation.summary: Roughly 1,600 people in the United States contract listeriosis each year and about 260 die of it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Every year, roughly 1,600 people in the U.S. contract listeriosis, and 260 die from the illness. Listeriosis is therefore uncommon but carries a strikingly high case fatality, on the order of one in six. That lethality is what drives aggressive food recalls when contamination is detected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This tenfold underestimate does not match the reported annual U.S. burden.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sixteen thousand cases overstates the incidence by an order of magnitude.

questions.stem: In 2024, the CDC reported a multistate listeriosis outbreak that infected 34 people and prompted a manufacturer to recall 7 million pounds of a single product. Interviews revealed that the majority of patients had eaten which of the following?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Raw oysters on the half shell

explanation.summary: The 2024 multistate listeriosis outbreak was traced to meats sliced at deli counters.
explanation.whyCorrect: In 2024, the CDC reported a multistate outbreak of listeriosis that infected 34 people, and interviews revealed that the majority of patients had eaten meats sliced at deli counters. Boar's Head recalled 7 million pounds of deli meat over contamination concerns. Processed and ready-to-eat meats are a recurring vehicle because Listeria continues to grow in refrigerated product.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Peaches have been subject to listeriosis-related recalls previously but were not the source described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cantaloupe has been recalled in past listeriosis outbreaks but was not the vehicle in the 2024 deli-counter outbreak.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bean sprouts have been implicated in earlier outbreaks and recalls, not in this one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Raw oysters are not among the foods linked to this organism's major outbreaks.
